learning_outcomes.text: Student knows the construction and operating principles of devices used in the place of professional practice and knows the basic principles of designing and/or manufacturing products of the chosen workplace.
Student has knowledge in the field of specialized issues of the chosen branch of electrical engineering, power engineering, control systems and measurement systems.
Is able to estimate the time needed to complete a delegated task and is able to develop and implement a work schedule to meet deadlines.
Is able to prepare and present a short presentation on the results of an engineering task.
Is aware of responsibility for their own work and readiness to comply with team work principles and take responsibility for jointly realized tasks.
Understands the need for continuous learning and improving professional competencies.

syllabus_topics: Professional placement. The purpose of the professional placement is to supplement the knowledge, skills, and social competencies acquired during studies with practical components characteristic of the student's placement location. The practical placement enables gaining experience in the field of electrical engineering, including: learning the specifics of an engineer's work in an environment similar to the graduate's future workplace, gaining experience through the implementation of practical tasks (under the supervision of an authorized person at the placement location), e.g., using theoretical knowledge from the current curriculum, learning basic methods, forms, and tools of work, learning the principles of organization and work planning and documentation management, gaining experience in independent and teamwork, familiarizing oneself with the requirements of future employers.

Place and time of placement. Students complete professional placements in companies with which the University has signed cooperation agreements for practical placements or in companies chosen by students after approval by the AGH placement supervisor. The placement location can be, among others, a production plant, energy plant, telecommunication plant, construction company, unit performing electrical and non-electrical measurements using electrical methods, etc., which would ensure the student's tasks are consistent with the Electrical Engineering curriculum. The practical placement cannot conflict with other classes planned in the study program and class schedule. The practical placement cannot be an excuse for absence from classes or exams. The total hourly dimension of the placement results from the syllabus entries, i.e., a total of 120 hours. Before the start of the summer examination session and before undertaking the placement, the student should: obtain the required consents from the Dean/Vice-Dean resulting from the applicable rules for student placements, choose a placement location, obtain the placement supervisor's approval regarding the chosen company and obtain consent from the company for undertaking the student placement, obtain accident insurance (NNW) and civil liability insurance (OC) valid during the placement period (if required by the company), provide the university placement supervisor with all necessary documents required for preparing a cooperation agreement and/or referral for the placement (e.g., written consent from the company for the student's chosen placement), provide the company (before the start of the placement) with the signed agreement and/or referral and any other documents required to start the placement. Detailed rules for organizing placements (e.g., list of required documents, credit deadlines) are determined by the university placement supervisor.

Placement implementation - framework program. Professional placements are carried out on the basis of a concluded cooperation agreement between AGH and the company or written consent from the company for the student placement. The placement is unpaid work for the given company. The scope of the intern's main duties should align with the study profile and the student's chosen education path in the areas of power engineering, power electronics and electrical drives, or automation and metrology. During the placement, the student should familiarize themselves with the company's business profile and guidelines for work organization, including: familiarizing themselves with regulations regarding safe and hygienic work (BHP), learning and observing the regulations, procedures, and work organization requirements applicable at the company, especially regarding working hours, order and discipline, and observing company secrets, data confidentiality, and personal data protection, familiarizing themselves with possible hazards occurring at the company, familiarizing themselves with the operating principles of the company's electrical power devices and fire protection principles, familiarizing themselves with the scope of work carried out at the company, learning the organizational structure of the company, the scope of authorization to issue instructions, and the responsibility of people in individual positions, etc. In terms of tasks performed during the placement (depending on the company's business profile), the student should: deepen their knowledge in the field related to the company's activities at the placement location, learn the technological processes carried out at the placement location, familiarize themselves with the technical devices used in technological processes, familiarize themselves with the assembly of electrical power devices, learn about the maintenance and diagnostics of electrical power machines and devices, familiarize themselves with available computer systems and programs used in production and design processes, familiarize themselves with the possibilities of expanding and modifying electrical power devices, systems, and networks, familiarize themselves with the protections used in power engineering, automation, drive systems, etc., participate in repair, measurement, assembly, equipment operation, etc., within the scope corresponding to possessed qualifications and skills, participate in solving technical problems arising from the implementation of a specific production process, measurement task, etc., independently solve delegated tasks within the scope of possessed skills and qualifications, participate in the implementation of group tasks resulting from the company's activities, acquiring skills in effective communication and teamwork, implement assigned tasks according to the designated schedule and within the designated time, familiarize themselves with methods of preparing technical documentation for electrical devices, as well as protocols and usage instructions, acquire skills in preparing reports and statements on performed work, obtain information on development trends in a given branch of production, services, construction, measurements, etc., learn the principles of economics and marketing (conditioned by the company's specifics), collect information regarding personally performed tasks, in order to keep a placement logbook or prepare a detailed report on the course of the placement.

After the placement, the student should: obtain a certificate from the company confirming the completion of the placement, prepare a detailed report on the course of the placement, report to the AGH placement supervisor for credit for the professional placement and submit the required documents for placement credit. The templates for the above-mentioned documents (agreements, certificates, consents, reports) are attachments to the Rector of AGH University of Krakow's current regulation on the principles of organizing student placements at AGH University of Krakow.
teaching_methods: Teaching methods and techniques used at a place where a practical placement is performed

assessment_methods.method: Report on completion of a practical placement
Confirmation of completion of practical placement programme

assessment_rules: To receive credit for the placement, the student must submit the Dean's/Vice-Dean's consent (if required), a certificate of completed placement from the workplace, and a detailed report according to the template. Credit is granted based on these documents, potentially supplemented by an interview with the supervisor about the placement's course and objectives. The report should characterize the company and detail the work done to enhance practical knowledge, with credit depending on the student's task completion, duties, and work performed, considering the practical possibilities at the placement site. Practical placements are graded as "zal." (credited) or "nzal." (not credited). If the placement is not completed or credited by the deadline, it can be undertaken and credited at a later date with written consent from the Dean/Vice-Dean.
